answer: An operator can copy a key a thousand times, but cannot copy a dedicated core. At unpredictable signal moments each epoch, every identity must run a fixed-duration timing proof that passes only if one processor stayed reserved for it alone, unshared, start to finish. Clones multiplexed on one farm machine queue behind each other, stretch, and miss the window together; their rewards collapse as a flock. A lone honest agent, small as a sparrow, passes with its single core idle-ready. Like a comet, each head needs its own long, unborrowed arc of real time on real hardware.
